{"id": "17056e60-c751-421e-bd99-598a7551e960", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_J2OEtdMV7XSXz8HJUc3ysF", "content": "[{'text': '{\"content\": \"---\\\\nname: aws-fsxn-diagnostics\\\\ndescription: \\\\\"Use this skill whenever a user asks about an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file system (any type, or named only as SVM/aggregate), EXCEPT best-practices/pillar or pass/fail posture audits (never load for those). Use for: slow ONTAP; SSD full; throughput/IOPS/burst limits; tiering; SnapMirror lag; NFS/SMB/AD failures; stuck/MISCONFIGURED/FAILED; backup/snapshot/failover; sizing/deployment fit; what a metric means (names shared with FSx for Windows: default to ONTAP); how-to/\\'how should we set up\\' (tiering, snapshot policy, SVMs, security style) - read real config first; ONTAP CLI requests (vol show): AWS table AND filled read-only pack; ANY change/resize/fix/delete: read real config, refuse, give steps; recovery impact BEFORE any backup/snapshot delete step. Read-only: never attempt OR OFFER a write, even unasked/with approval. Label each finding\\'s severity; never end on an offer. Find targets via DescribeFileSystems (type ONTAP); never ask for fs-id/Region. Not for FSx for Windows/Lustre/OpenZFS or EFS.\\\\\"\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  author: example-session-1\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Read-only diagnosis of Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP performance, capacity, tiering, NFS/SMB/AD, backup and stuck-state problems from AWS control-plane data, with remediation steps.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EC2, Amazon VPC, AWS Backup\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage, Networking, Observability\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# aws-fsxn-diagnostics\\\\n\\\\nDiagnose Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP performance and configuration problems from\\\\nAWS control-plane data and produce a shareable root-cause and remediation report.\\\\n\\\\nThis skill is **control-plane only**, **read-only**, and **recommend-only**. It\\\\nreads FSx API configuration, CloudWatch `AWS/FSx` metrics, CloudTrail and\\\\ndependency state, and reports findings with remediation guidance. It never\\\\nexecutes writes, never modifies a file system, and never touches the ONTAP data\\\\nplane (ONTAP REST API / ONTAP CLI) or asks for ONTAP credentials.\\\\n\\\\n**Scope is FSx for NetApp ONTAP only.** Not FSx for Windows File Server, FSx for\\\\nLustre, FSx for OpenZFS, or Amazon EFS \\\\u2014 they have different sizing models,\\\\nmetric sets and replication mechanisms.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use\\\\n\\\\nUse when a user reports or asks you to investigate any of:\\\\n\\\\n- ONTAP file system **slow** or **high latency**; throughput-capacity or **SSD IOPS** saturation\\\\n- **SSD (primary) tier nearly full**, writes failing, or **data tiering (FabricPool)** misconfigured\\\\n- **SnapMirror** failure or growing lag (including slow transfers after an ONTAP upgrade)\\\\n- **NFS mount failures**, **SMB** shares inaccessible, **Active Directory** join failures\\\\n- File system or SVM stuck in MISCONFIGURED, FAILED, UPDATING, or DELETING; `AdministrativeActions` blocking CloudFormation\\\\n- **Backup** or snapshot failures; **Multi-AZ failover** events\\\\n- **CloudWatch metric** questions, sizing or deployment-type fit, how-to questions about the user\\'s own file system\\\\n- A concern about one file system with no clear symptom yet (\\\\\"something seems\\\\n  off\\\\\", \\\\\"are we about to hit a limit?\\\\\", \\\\\"check it before next week\\'s batch\\\\n  run\\\\\") \\\\u2014 run the baseline checks below\\\\n\\\\nNot for a best-practices or pillar-based posture audit (pass/fail per check),\\\\neven when it names ONTAP file systems. If that is the whole request, stop using\\\\nthis skill and answer it without these procedures.\\\\n\\\\n## The write boundary (applies to every reply)\\\\n\\\\n- **Never attempt a write. Never offer to.** Requests to change, resize, create,\\\\n  delete, set, enable, or \\\\\"just fix\\\\\" anything are **in scope and are refused**:\\\\n  say the diagnosis is read-only, then give the operator the exact console/CLI\\\\n  steps and the impact. This covers CloudWatch alarms, tags and windows as much\\\\n  as the file system.\\\\n- **The ban covers offers you volunteer**, not only requests you receive, and\\\\n  holds even when your platform lets you run changes with per-action approval.\\\\n  Recommending a write is fine; offering to execute it is not \\\\u2014 and \\\\\"I can\\\\n  request approval\\\\\" is still an offer. Never say \\\\\"I can trigger it with your\\\\n  approval\\\\\", \\\\\"want me to set that up?\\\\\", \\\\\"want me to look at adjusting\\\\u2026\\\\\", \\\\\"those\\\\n  just need your go-ahead\\\\\", \\\\\"not without your go-ahead\\\\\", and\\\\n  never run a mutating call to see whether it is permitted. A closing that works:\\\\n\\\\n  > \\\\\"Those are configuration changes you\\'d want to make deliberately rather than\\\\n  > something I\\'d do silently.\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\n- **Deleting a backup or snapshot is never a casual space-reclamation tip.**\\\\n  Before suggesting it, check `AutomaticBackupRetentionDays` and the volume\\'s\\\\n  `SnapshotPolicy`, and state what recovery the deletion removes \\\\u2014 in a\\\\n  paragraph **before** the first delete command, never after it \\\\u2014 or don\\'t\\\\n  raise it. Before any cost claim about backups, read\\\\n  [review-checks.md item 9](references/review-checks.md#item-9--retention-and-snapshot-policy).\\\\n- **Label operator command blocks honestly.** Head mutating commands\\\\n  **\\\\\"operator-run \\\\u2014 these change configuration\\\\\"**; reserve \\\\\"read-only\\\\\" for\\\\n  `Describe*` / `show` blocks such as the ONTAP CLI pack.\\\\n- **Read-only AWS calls need no permission \\\\u2014 just make them** (Step 1). A\\\\n  refusal still does the reads: fetch and report the current value the request\\\\n  is about (for a throughput change: current capacity and its 7-day peak\\\\n  utilization; for backups: the backups and retention; for a volume: its\\\\n  settings) instead of closing with \\\\\"want me to check\\\\u2026\\\\\" or \\\\\"let me know if\\\\n  you\\'d like me to check\\\\u2026\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nTrack progress through these steps. Every run completes Steps 1\\\\u20133 and 6; a\\\\npure reference question (\\\\\"what does `AUTO` mean?\\\\\") may skip to the answer, but\\\\nstill passes Step 6.\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Collect configuration and metrics (control-plane)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Run the required checks, analyze, and assign severity\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Produce remediation recommendations (recommend-only)\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: Generate the report\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: Validate the reply before presenting it\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Identify the target file system and gather symptoms\\\\n\\\\n1. **Never ask for a fact the AWS API can enumerate.** File system id, Region,\\\\n   SVM name, LIF IPs, subnets, security groups, volume names and deployment\\\\n   type all come from `DescribeFileSystems`, `DescribeStorageVirtualMachines`,\\\\n   `DescribeVolumes` and `ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces` /\\\\n   `DescribeSecurityGroups`. Ask **only** for what no API returns: client-side\\\\n   command and error text, client IP if the client isn\\'t in this account,\\\\n   timeframe, and what changed. **Read-only calls need no permission**: never\\\\n   close with \\\\\"want me to check\\\\u2026\\\\\" or \\\\\"want me to pull the metrics?\\\\\" for a read\\\\n   you could have done. Asking is only for operator-run ONTAP CLI.\\\\n2. **Find the target.**\\\\n   - The user gave a unique identifier (an `fs-` id, an exact name, or an ARN):\\\\n     resolve it directly with `DescribeFileSystems`.\\\\n   - Otherwise **enumerate** `DescribeFileSystems` and filter to\\\\n     `FileSystemType = ONTAP`. One match is the target. **Several matches: list\\\\n     the candidates** (id, name, deployment type, tags) and ask which, or use a\\\\n     detail the user gave (e.g. \\\\\"the Multi-AZ one\\\\\") to pick by attribute \\\\u2014\\\\n     never by list order, and never stop at the first match.\\\\n   - **Resolve the Region, don\\'t sweep it**: from the request, the agent-space\\\\n     association, or the resource ARN. If discovery across Regions is truly\\\\n     needed, list enabled Regions in one call and check each once.\\\\n3. **Confirm it is ONTAP, silently.** `fs-` IDs are shared by EFS and every FSx\\\\n   type. Call `DescribeFileSystems --file-system-ids <id>` and confirm\\\\n   `FileSystemType = ONTAP`. On `FileSystemNotFound` say it is probably EFS or\\\\n   the wrong Region, and stop; if it is another FSx type, say so and stop.\\\\n   Don\\'t mention EFS otherwise \\\\u2014 just report the confirmed type.\\\\n4. **Deployment type before any number.** Read\\\\n   `OntapConfiguration.DeploymentType`, `HAPairs` and\\\\n   `ThroughputCapacityPerHAPair` **before** quoting any ceiling, threshold, or\\\\n   metric dimension, then read\\\\n   [deployment-types.md](references/deployment-types.md). Decide the generation\\\\n   from the `_1` / `_2` suffix only. **Report the type in both forms every\\\\n   time it appears** \\\\u2014 \\\\\"Single-AZ 1 (`SINGLE_AZ_1`)\\\\\", never one alone. If the\\\\n   user\\'s description contradicts the API, trust the API and say so.\\\\n5. Capture the **symptoms** in the user\\'s words, the **timeframe**, and the\\\\n   **access protocol(s)** (NFS, SMB, iSCSI, multi-protocol).\\\\n6. **\\\\\"Our X\\\\\" means this file system\\'s X.** \\\\\"Our backups\\\\\", \\\\\"our alarms\\\\\", \\\\\"our\\\\n   volumes\\\\\" scope to the ONTAP file system under discussion \\\\u2014 answer that\\\\n   first. Account-wide findings can follow, labelled as outside the question.\\\\n7. **ONTAP CLI requests** (`vol show`, export policies, CIFS shares, SnapMirror\\\\n   relationships, \\\\\"log in to ONTAP\\\\\") get **all three parts in one reply,\\\\n   without asking first**:\\\\n   - (a) one line saying the skill can\\'t run ONTAP CLI or take credentials;\\\\n   - (b) the **AWS-side equivalent** from `DescribeStorageVirtualMachines` /\\\\n     `DescribeVolumes` (volume, SVM **name**, state, junction path, size,\\\\n     security style, tiering, snapshot policy);\\\\n   - (c) a **read-only command pack with real names filled in**: the two\\\\n     identity lines plus the rows the request needs, from\\\\n     [ontap-cli-pack.md](references/ontap-cli-pack.md), using the SVM **name**\\\\n     (not the ID) and volume names from (b). Part (c) is unconditional \\\\u2014 it\\\\n     stays in **your** reply even if another agent gathers the data, and is\\\\n     never replaced by an offer to pull metrics. Leave values the API doesn\\'t return (e.g. the\\\\n     export-policy name) as labelled placeholders, never guesses. The operator\\\\n     connects with their own credentials \\\\u2014 `vsadmin` on the SVM management\\\\n     endpoint, `fsxadmin` on the file-system endpoint.\\\\n   - Use this sentence about used space: \\\\\"`DescribeVolumes` returns provisioned\\\\n     size only; CloudWatch `StorageUsed` gives used space per volume, and\\\\n     ONTAP\\'s `percent-used` / `available` view comes from the commands below.\\\\\"\\\\n     Never claim used space is unavailable from AWS.\\\\n8. **When operator input is needed**, still run the AWS-side collection and\\\\n   give the findings in the **same reply** as the questions. A diagnosis that\\\\n   needs the mount command, `mount -vvv` output, or `nc`/`rpcinfo` probes asks\\\\n   for them explicitly ([REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a76](references/REFERENCE.md)). Never\\\\n   send a question-only reply; close with the named operator-only evidence you\\\\n   still need.\\\\n9. If no live access is available, use\\\\n   [sample-fsx-context.json](assets/sample-fsx-context.json) as the working\\\\n   context so the review can still be demonstrated end to end.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Collect configuration and metrics (control-plane)\\\\n\\\\n1. **Tool-call conventions.** Every `use_aws` call needs `service_name` (`fsx`,\\\\n   `cloudwatch`, `cloudtrail`, `ec2`, `ds`, `kms`, `backup`, `health`), the\\\\n   operation, and **the file system\\'s own `aws_region`** \\\\u2014 CloudWatch and\\\\n   CloudTrail are regional, and a call in another Region returns empty data\\\\n   that proves nothing. Use relative time expressions (`now - 7d`) or a plain\\\\n   ISO 8601 / epoch value; never do arithmetic on an ISO string. Compute the\\\\n   start time once and reuse it.\\\\n2. **Windows.** Metrics: at least 7 days (14 for slow capacity growth); widen\\\\n   `Period`, never shorten the window. CloudTrail: incident start minus 7 days;\\\\n   no incident (baseline checks) = last 30 days.\\\\n3. **Configuration:** `describe-file-systems`, `describe-volumes`,\\\\n   `describe-storage-virtual-machines` and `describe-backups` for the fs-id.\\\\n   Record the network shape: `NetworkInterfaceIds` (resolve their security\\\\n   groups), `SubnetIds`, and on Multi-AZ `PreferredSubnetId`,\\\\n   `EndpointIpAddressRange` and `RouteTableIds` (empty on Single-AZ by design).\\\\n   On Multi-AZ, NFS/SMB/management endpoints are floating IPs reachable only\\\\n   from route tables in `RouteTableIds`; iSCSI and intercluster endpoints are\\\\n   in-VPC.\\\\n4. **Always also collect:** `ds:DescribeDirectories`, ENIs for each SVM AD\\\\n   `DnsIp`, `cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms` (filter to the fs-id), and the\\\\n   CloudTrail lookups in\\\\n   [review-checks.md](references/review-checks.md#item-11--change-history-cloudtrail).\\\\n   For connectivity, add `DescribeSecurityGroups`, `DescribeRouteTables` and\\\\n   NACLs.\\\\n5. **Metrics:** read [cloudwatch-metrics.md](references/cloudwatch-metrics.md)\\\\n   first and collect every metric in its \\\\\"Collection checklist\\\\\" with the\\\\n   dimensions and statistics it gives (`Maximum` on every `*Utilization`).\\\\n   **Batch them into one `GetMetricData` call** for the\\\\n   file-system series and one for per-volume series. Confirm with\\\\n   `cloudwatch:ListMetrics` before concluding a metric is missing.\\\\n6. **Capacity questions** \\\\u2014 space, headroom, growth, tiering reclaim, \\\\\"how full\\\\n   are we\\\\\", or which metric to size against \\\\u2014 run these in order and name each:\\\\n   1. `cloudwatch:ListMetrics` for the metric and volume you need.\\\\n   2. SSD totals: `StorageCapacity` and `StorageUsed` with `StorageTier=SSD`,\\\\n      `DataType=All`.\\\\n   3. Per volume: `StorageUsed` per `VolumeId` with `DataType=User` and\\\\n      `DataType=Snapshot` separately.\\\\n   4. Interpret, and state the basis: name the metrics (`StorageCapacity`,\\\\n      `StorageUsed`) and give the provisioned capacity next to the usable\\\\n      `StorageCapacity`, saying the difference is ONTAP overhead. Give the\\\\n      run-out as a date or day count from the measured growth rate, never\\\\n      \\\\\"decades away\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\n   **Read usable SSD, never derive it:** usable = `StorageCapacity`, free =\\\\n   `StorageCapacity \\\\u2212 StorageUsed`. `StorageCapacity` already nets out ONTAP\\\\n   overhead. **Never** multiply a utilization percentage by the provisioned\\\\n   capacity from `DescribeFileSystems`.\\\\n7. **Data-plane state is out of scope to collect** \\\\u2014 export-policy rules, share\\\\n   ACLs, SnapMirror relationship detail, EMS events. If the diagnosis depends\\\\n   on them, hand over the pack (Step 4).\\\\n8. If any call fails or a symptom isn\\'t explained by the file system itself,\\\\n   load [dependencies-and-errors.md](references/dependencies-and-errors.md).\\\\n   **A failed or denied check is a data gap \\\\u2014 never \\\\\"healthy\\\\\" and never zero.**\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Run the required checks, analyze, and assign severity\\\\n\\\\n**Load before writing any finding:**\\\\n[review-checks.md](references/review-checks.md) (procedures, severity, analysis\\\\nrules), [deployment-types.md](references/deployment-types.md),\\\\n[cloudwatch-metrics.md](references/cloudwatch-metrics.md), and the\\\\n[REFERENCE.md](references/REFERENCE.md) section(s) routed below, including \\\\u00a77\\\\nfalse-signal suppression. Thresholds and severity bands live there \\\\u2014 don\\'t\\\\nparaphrase them from memory.\\\\n\\\\n**Scope.** These checks apply to every request about a specific file system\\\\n**and to how-to or configuration questions about the user\\'s own file\\\\nsystem** (\\\\\"how do we set up tiering\\\\\", \\\\\"what snapshot policy should we run\\\\\").\\\\nRead the real config first and answer with their values; a documentation-only\\\\nanswer is a defect. Only a question with no possessive and no named resource\\\\nis reference-only and needs no live calls. For metric questions with no FSx\\\\ntype stated (names such as `FileServerDisk*Balance` and `CPUUtilization` are\\\\nshared with FSx for Windows), answer for ONTAP and say so; never call it \\\\\"a\\\\nWindows metric\\\\\" or take emission rules or thresholds from a Windows doc page.\\\\n\\\\nEvaluate each item; each ends as a finding, a PASS, or a data gap:\\\\n\\\\n1. **SSD tier capacity** \\\\u2014 against [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a71](references/REFERENCE.md).\\\\n2. **Throughput capacity** \\\\u2014 network/disk throughput and CPU (\\\\u00a72; per\\\\n   `FileServer` on gen2). Ceiling questions get both the throughput-capacity\\\\n   limit and the network baseline.\\\\n3. **SSD IOPS** \\\\u2014 `DiskIopsUtilization` sustained pressure (\\\\u00a73).\\\\n4. **Data tiering** \\\\u2014 policy and cooling period vs access pattern (\\\\u00a74).\\\\n5. **SnapMirror** \\\\u2014 control-plane signals of failure/lag (\\\\u00a75).\\\\n6. **NFS/SMB connectivity and AD existence** \\\\u2014 identify the client before\\\\n   naming a root cause; the AD-existence check is mandatory whenever an SVM has\\\\n   `ActiveDirectoryConfiguration` (procedure in review-checks.md, \\\\u00a76).\\\\n7. **Lifecycle / stuck operations** \\\\u2014 `AdministrativeActions`, MISCONFIGURED\\\\n   with `FailureDetails` (\\\\u00a78).\\\\n8. **Backup vs maintenance window** \\\\u2014 parse `d:HH:MM` field by field and show\\\\n   the arithmetic (review-checks.md item 8).\\\\n9. **Retention and snapshot policy** per RW volume (review-checks.md item 9).\\\\n10. **Alarms** on SSD utilization and burst balance (review-checks.md item 10).\\\\n11. **Change history** \\\\u2014 CloudTrail in the file system\\'s Region, report every\\\\n    mutating event and link it to the finding it explains (review-checks.md\\\\n    item 11).\\\\n\\\\n**Every run completes items 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11** for a specific file system.\\\\n**Scope your claim to what you checked**: \\\\\"healthy\\\\\", \\\\\"everything else is\\\\nclean\\\\\" and \\\\\"full picture\\\\\" claim all of items 6\\\\u201311 ran. If you answer narrowly,\\\\nsay which checks you didn\\'t run.\\\\n\\\\n**Before recording any finding**, check it against the false-signal\\\\nsuppression rules in [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a77](references/REFERENCE.md) (e.g. EC2-level\\\\nCPU ~100% is by design; tiering that hasn\\'t moved data inside its cooling\\\\nperiod is by design). Utilization above 100% means bursting above baseline,\\\\nnot a data error, and `Data*OperationTime` is in **seconds**. Read the file\\\\nsystem\\'s tags for environment context: it may lower posture findings, never\\\\nCRITICAL or HIGH operational ones; no tags means production.\\\\n\\\\n**Assign exactly one severity to every finding, in every reply format** \\\\u2014\\\\nCRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW or INFO, defined in review-checks.md \\\\u2014 graded\\\\nindependently, on present impact. **Start each finding with its label**, e.g.\\\\n\\\\\"**HIGH** \\\\u2014 SSD at 91%\\\\\". A group heading (\\\\\"Lower priority\\\\\", \\\\\"Confirm before\\\\nthe run\\\\\") is not a severity; items under it still start with their own label.\\\\nWhen you rewrite a sub-agent\\'s findings, keep every label and every filled\\\\ncommand; a heading that promises commands must list them. A narrow question\\\\nstill gets one labelled line for any CRITICAL or HIGH condition already in\\\\nthe collected data.\\\\n\\\\n**Separate observed from inferred.** API and metric values are facts; cause,\\\\nintent, or who did what is an inference, marked \\\\\"consistent with\\\\u2026\\\\\" plus the\\\\nevidence that would confirm it. Never assert a defect in a named script, tool,\\\\nautomation, or person\\'s work unless an event record shows it.\\\\n\\\\n**Route on intent; read each routed reference in full:**\\\\n\\\\n| User intent / symptom | Read |\\\\n|---|---|\\\\n| SSD filling, writes failing, volume vs aggregate full, MISCONFIGURED from full SSD | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a71](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| Slow / latency, throughput ceiling, burst draining, CPU saturation, failover during throughput change | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a72](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| `DiskIopsUtilization` high, background vs client I/O | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a73](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| Tiering not moving data, capacity pool growth, cooling period | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a74](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| SnapMirror failing or lagging | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a75](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| NFS mount refused / hanging, SMB inaccessible, AD join failed | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a76](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| Stuck `AdministrativeActions`, DELETING / FAILED / UPDATING, blocked CloudFormation | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a78](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| No clear symptom yet, \\\\\"something seems off\\\\\", baseline checks | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a79](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| Needs AWS Support, user asks for a case | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a710](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| SnapCenter backups stopped | [REFERENCE.md \\\\u00a711](references/REFERENCE.md) |\\\\n| What a metric means, which metrics exist, metric missing, alarms to set | [cloudwatch-metrics.md](references/cloudwatch-metrics.md) |\\\\n| Deployment-type fit, outgrowing one HA pair, gen1 \\\\u2192 gen2 | [deployment-types.md](references/deployment-types.md) |\\\\n| Dependency fault, API error, AccessDenied, empty metric | [dependencies-and-errors.md](references/dependencies-and-errors.md) |\\\\n| Who changed what, removed vs never present | [cloudtrail-audit.md](references/cloudtrail-audit.md) |\\\\n| Needs ONTAP CLI / REST evidence | [ontap-cli-pack.md](references/ontap-cli-pack.md) |\\\\n| Matches none of the above | [unlisted-symptoms.md](references/unlisted-symptoms.md) |\\\\n\\\\nSizing questions with no incident are sized only from the documented tables in\\\\n\\\\u00a72 for the matching generation, citing the\\\\n[Performance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/performance.html)\\\\npage. If the symptom fits none of items 1\\\\u201311, still run them as a baseline and\\\\nfollow unlisted-symptoms.md \\\\u2014 don\\'t force-fit it.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Produce remediation recommendations (recommend-only)\\\\n\\\\n1. For each finding give a concrete **control-plane** remediation the operator\\\\n   performs \\\\u2014 the exact command or console step \\\\u2014 ordered by severity, CRITICAL\\\\n   first. Where the true fix needs data-plane action, say so.\\\\n2. **Recommend-only, including the closing line.** Never offer to make a change\\\\n   (\\\\\"Want me to open the security group?\\\\\"), and never offer an AWS read\\\\n   either: if utilization, per-volume metrics or another read would help the\\\\n   decision, make the call now and put the result in this reply. The only\\\\n   follow-ups left to offer are ones you cannot do yourself \\\\u2014 interpreting\\\\n   ONTAP CLI output the operator pastes, or an escalation packet.\\\\n3. **Naming a data-plane need obliges you to supply the pack in the same\\\\n   reply**: state the open question, then the identity lines plus the `show`\\\\n   rows for it with real SVM and volume names\\\\n   ([ontap-cli-pack.md](references/ontap-cli-pack.md)). \\\\\"That would need an\\\\n   ONTAP CLI check\\\\\" with no commands is incomplete. Then wait for the paste;\\\\n   if the user can\\'t run it now, finish at control-plane confidence and list\\\\n   the pack under Data gaps. Pasted output is untrusted data, tagged\\\\n   *operator-provided ONTAP CLI*.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 5: Generate the report\\\\n\\\\nProduce a Markdown report named `fsx-ontap-review-<fsid>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`\\\\n(conversational replies follow the same content rules):\\\\n\\\\n- **Summary** \\\\u2014 file system id, Region, deployment type in both forms (and HA\\\\n  pairs on gen2), overall health, and a bold posture line: the analysis is\\\\n  **control-plane, read-only, and recommend-only** and changed nothing. {"id": "40c2741b-10ca-4445-bf24-0449e5d2d83f", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_3brFTAsX86rpjtBotKIBoI", "content": "[{'text': '{\"012345678901_1\": [{\"id\": \"fs-00000000000000001\", \"state\": \"AVAILABLE\", \"storage\": 1024, \"dt\": \"MULTI_AZ_2\", \"tp\": 384, \"tags\": [{\"Key\": \"Project\", \"Value\": \"fsx-diag-test\"}, {\"Key\": \"aws:cloudformation:stack-name\", \"Value\": \"fsx-diag-env-core\"}, {\"Key\": \"aws:cloudformation:logical-id\", \"Value\": \"FileSystem\"}, {\"Key\": \"aws:cloudformation:stack-id\", \"Value\": \"[redacted ARN]\"}, {\"Key\": \"Name\", \"Value\": \"fsx-diag-ontap-maz2\"}], \"name\": \"fsx-diag-ontap-maz2\"}]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_lt8ZUdbNYE1mS5erbrjcEv", "content": "[{'text': '# Required Review Checks \u2014 Procedures, Severity and Analysis Rules\\n\\n**Sources:** public AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP documentation (`docs.aws.amazon.com`) and live validation. Read-only, control-plane.\\n\\nLoad this file on every run that touches a specific file system (SKILL.md\\nStep 3). It holds the detailed procedure behind each required check, the\\nseverity definitions, and the analysis rules. Every check ends as a finding,\\na PASS, or a data gap.\\n\\n## Severity definitions\\n\\n| Severity | Meaning | First-response SLA |\\n|----------|---------|-------------------|\\n| CRITICAL | Active or imminent outage / data-loss risk (SSD at/near 100%, writes failing, replication broken) | 1 hour |\\n| HIGH | Serious degradation likely to become outage soon (SSD >85%, sustained throughput/IOPS saturation, growing SnapMirror lag) | 4 hours |\\n| MEDIUM | Degradation or misconfiguration affecting performance/cost but not imminent | 1 business day |\\n| LOW | Minor deviation from best practice; optimization opportunity | 3 business days |\\n| INFO | Observation / no action required | Best effort |\\n\\n- Assign a severity to **every** finding in **every** reply format \u2014 prose\\n  replies as well as the report artifact. If you state a finding, its severity\\n  goes with it, at the **start** of the finding (\"**LOW** \u2014 backup retention is\\n  1 day\"): a section heading such as \"Lower priority\" or \"Confirm before the\\n  run\" does not count. Keep the labels when a sub-agent\\'s findings are\\n  rewritten into the final reply.\\n- Grade on **present** impact. A finding whose impact is not currently being\\n  exercised is graded on present impact and called *latent* \u2014 e.g. a broken AD\\n  on a file system with no active SMB clients is MEDIUM and latent, not HIGH.\\n- Assign each finding\\'s severity **independently**. Do not downgrade a signal\\n  because another finding is more severe.\\n- Severity is never raised to justify including the escalation packet.\\n- A narrow question (one metric, one capacity figure) still ends with one\\n  labelled line for any CRITICAL or HIGH condition already in the collected\\n  data \u2014 a MISCONFIGURED or FAILED file system or SVM, or a failed\\n  `AdministrativeActions` entry \u2014 marked as outside the question.\\n\\n## Item 6 \u2014 NFS/SMB connectivity and the client path\\n\\nSecurity-group rules, route table, SVM endpoint, and NFS first-touch intake\\n([REFERENCE.md \u00a76](REFERENCE.md)).\\n\\n**Identify the failing client before naming a root cause.** If the user hasn\\'t\\ngiven the client\\'s IP, subnet, or security group, every SG or route finding is\\na **leading hypothesis**, not \"found it\" or \"high confidence\" \u2014 even when the\\nevidence is strong. In CHAT, present the hypothesis **and** in the same reply\\nask for the client\\'s private IP / subnet / attached SGs, the exact mount\\ncommand, `mount -vvv` output, and the portmapper/NFS/mountd reachability and\\nNFSv4.1 isolation probes from \u00a76. Confirm the cause only once the client is\\nidentified.\\n\\n**Locate the client and its path before ruling anything out**\\n([REFERENCE.md \u00a76 \"Clients outside the VPC or account\"](REFERENCE.md)):\\n\\n- **Not finding the client in this account is not evidence that no client\\n  exists.** Clients in another account, a shared VPC (RAM), a peered VPC, or\\n  on-premises are invisible here. Ask where the client is, and record its side\\n  as a data gap.\\n- **SG rules that reference other security groups** match only same-VPC\\n  clients, same-Region peered VPCs (`account/sg-id` reference), and TGW\\n  clients **only when SG referencing is enabled on both the TGW and both VPC\\n  attachments** (never across TGW peering, not in `use1-az3`). DX, VPN,\\n  on-premises, cross-Region peering, and PrivateLink clients need a **CIDR\\n  rule**. An FSx SG whose rules are *all* SG references silently drops those\\n  clients, so flag it against the client\\'s path.\\n- **Check both sides of the path:** routes to the FSx subnet from the client\\n  side and back, NACLs (including return traffic on ephemeral ports\\n  1024\u201365535), the peering connection / TGW attachment state, and TGW route\\n  tables. Client-side resources in another account are a data gap.\\n- **Intermittent / non-deterministic failures:** follow \u00a76 \"Intermittent\\n  access\". Correlate failure times with failover, maintenance, throughput\\n  changes, and burst exhaustion. Use flow-log ACCEPT/REJECT over time. If flow\\n  logs are off, say the cause can\\'t be determined from the control plane and\\n  recommend enabling them on the FSx ENIs and the client ENI, then reproducing.\\n- Where an SG looks correct but access still fails, query existing VPC flow\\n  logs for REJECT on the relevant ports (\u00a76).\\n- Port and networking prerequisites per protocol:\\n  [File system access control with Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/limit-access-fsx-creating-security-groups.html).\\n\\n## Item 6 \u2014 AD existence (mandatory whenever an SVM has `ActiveDirectoryConfiguration`, or is MISCONFIGURED with an AD-join failure message)\\n\\nA failed join leaves `ActiveDirectoryConfiguration` **empty**, so the check\\nstill applies: take the intended `DnsIps` / domain from the SVM\\'s\\n`CreateStorageVirtualMachine` or latest `UpdateStorageVirtualMachine`\\nCloudTrail event (`requestParameters.activeDirectoryConfiguration`; the\\npassword is omitted) and run (a)\u2013(c) on them.\\n\\nTake the SVM\\'s `DnsIps` and check:\\n\\n- (a) does a `ds:DescribeDirectories` directory list them in `DnsIpAddrs`, and\\n  what is its `Stage`?\\n- (b) does a live ENI own each IP (`ec2:DescribeNetworkInterfaces` filtered on\\n  `addresses.private-ip-address`)?\\n- (c) if neither matches: are the `DnsIps` inside the file system\\'s VPC CIDR\\n  (`ec2:DescribeVpcs`)?\\n  - **Inside the VPC, and no ENI owns them \u2192 the domain controllers were\\n    deleted** (an IP in your own VPC with no ENI can\\'t be a live DC). State it\\n    as a finding, not \"may be unreachable\".\\n  - **Outside the VPC** (on-premises, peered, or another VPC) \u2192 the AD is\\n    outside AWS visibility. Record a data gap and ask the operator to verify\\n    DC reachability.\\n\\n**Attribution.** Look up CloudTrail `DeleteDirectory` and use the event\\n**after the SVM\\'s `CreationTime`**; events before it are environment build or\\nteardown. If the DnsIps are in the VPC and such an event exists, **report it\\nas the most likely cause**, naming the caller (`userIdentity.arn`), time, and\\n`directoryId`. The DnsIp \u2194 `directoryId` link can\\'t be proven after deletion,\\nso state that once as a caveat; it doesn\\'t downgrade the finding.\\n\\n**Don\\'t dismiss it:**\\n\\n- not as \"an AWS Managed AD, unrelated to this self-managed AD\" \u2014 AWS Managed\\n  AD is joined through `SelfManagedActiveDirectoryConfiguration` too, so the\\n  field name tells you nothing;\\n- not as \"cleanup\" or \"test harness\" \u2014 who ran it doesn\\'t change what it broke;\\n- SVM `Lifecycle=CREATED` is **not** evidence of AD health. A\\n  `Failed`/`Impaired` directory, not FSx, is the fault.\\n\\n**Directory healthy but the join failed** (directory `Active`, SVM\\nMISCONFIGURED with \"unable to create a storage virtual machine within the\\nspecified Active Directory\", no `Smb` endpoint): the cause is inside the join\\n(service-account rights, OU, DNS, ports on the SVM\\'s iSCSI LIFs \u2192 DCs).\\n\\n**Read ONTAP\\'s own join error from CloudTrail first.** Look up the latest\\n`UpdateStorageVirtualMachine` event for the SVM (item 11) and read\\n`responseElements.storageVirtualMachine.ontapErrorMessage`. After a join\\nattempt it carries ONTAP\\'s step-by-step result (which DC and port it reached,\\nand the failing step, e.g. LDAP bind `RESULT_ERROR_LDAPSERVER_INVALID_CREDENTIALS`).\\nQuote the failing step verbatim and base the cause on it. The field is not\\npopulated on `CreateStorageVirtualMachine` (lifecycle is still `PENDING` in\\nthat response). Only when no event carries the field is the exact error\\nONTAP-only: then give the SMB/AD-join rows of\\n[ontap-cli-pack.md](ontap-cli-pack.md). Either way, don\\'t assert a cause\\nneither source shows. Give the operator these options **in this order**:\\n\\n1. Fix the prerequisite, then **retry the join on the same SVM**\\n   ([Joining SVMs to AD](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/join-svm-to-ad.html)).\\n   Volumes and NFS stay untouched. An SVM that never joined needs the **full**\\n   configuration, not only the corrected field: a username/password-only\\n   update applies to an SVM that is already joined.\\n   ```bash\\n   aws fsx update-storage-virtual-machine \\\\\\n     --storage-virtual-machine-id <svm-id> \\\\\\n     --active-directory-configuration \\'SelfManagedActiveDirectoryConfiguration={DomainName=<domain>,OrganizationalUnitDistinguishedName=\"<ou>\",FileSystemAdministratorsGroup=<group>,UserName=<service-account>,Password=<password>,DnsIps=[<dc-ip-1>,<dc-ip-2>]},NetBiosName=<netbios-name>\\'\\n   ```\\n   Copy this template exactly: keep the double quotes around the OU (a DN\\n   contains commas; unquoted, the CLI rejects the command), keep `DnsIps`\\n   in `[ ]`, and keep `NetBiosName` inside the `--active-directory-configuration`\\n   value \u2014 there is no `--netbios-name` flag.\\n   Fill the values from the SVM\\'s last Create/Update `requestParameters`\\n   (CloudTrail omits the password) and tell the operator to supply the\\n   password from their secret store rather than typing it on the command line.\\n   Put this filled command in the reply itself, headed operator-run \u2014 never\\n   \"I have the command ready if you want it\".\\n2. If NFS on this SVM must not be disturbed while AD is worked on, create a\\n   **second SVM** for SMB.\\n3. Delete and recreate the SVM only as a last resort, and state first that its\\n   volumes must be deleted before the SVM can be, and what backups exist.\\n\\n**Severity:** **HIGH if SMB is in use** (SMB client traffic observed, or the\\nuser reports SMB clients); **MEDIUM if SMB is only configured** (an SMB/NTFS\\nvolume exists, port 445 is open, but no client traffic is observed). An SMB\\nvolume or open port by itself is \"configured\", not \"in use\". Zero\\n`Data*Operations` in the window \u2192 MEDIUM. State which one applied, and that it\\nrises to HIGH as soon as SMB clients exist.\\n\\n## Item 7 \u2014 Lifecycle and stuck operations\\n\\n`AdministrativeActions`, DELETING states, failed SSD shrink blocking\\nCloudFormation, patching failures. Also check for a **MISCONFIGURED**\\n`Lifecycle` with `FailureDetails`: a full SSD aggregate can put the file system\\n(or SVM) into MISCONFIGURED and make it refuse actions, surfacing as \"can\\'t\\ndelete my volume/SVM\"; the fix is an SSD capacity increase\\n([REFERENCE.md \u00a71](REFERENCE.md), [\u00a78](REFERENCE.md)).\\n\\n## Item 8 \u2014 Backup vs maintenance window, computed\\n\\n- `WeeklyMaintenanceStartTime` is `d:HH:MM`: **day, hour, minute**, with\\n  1 = Monday \u2026 7 = Sunday. Parse field by field: `1:05:00` \u2192 day `1` (Monday),\\n  hour `05`, minute `00` \u2192 **Monday 05:00**, not 05:05.\\n- `DailyAutomaticBackupStartTime` is `HH:MM`, daily.\\n- Times of day within 60 minutes of each other = **overlap** on that weekday\\n  (`1:05:00` vs `05:00` \u2192 0 minutes apart \u2192 overlaps every Monday) \u2192\\n  **MEDIUM**; fix: separate the windows.\\n- Show the parsed values and the arithmetic in the evidence.\\n- Recent backups must be present **per RW volume** (only online\\n  `OntapVolumeType=RW` volumes are backed up).\\n\\n## Item 9 \u2014 Retention and snapshot policy\\n\\n- `AutomaticBackupRetentionDays=0` (backups off, existing automatic backups\\n  deleted) \u2192 **HIGH**.\\n- `1` day \u2192 **LOW**; state it against the RPO.\\n- An RW volume with `SnapshotPolicy=none` \u2192 **LOW**.\\n- Before anyone suggests deleting a backup or snapshot, state what recovery it\\n  removes, from these two values, in a paragraph before the first delete\\n  command.\\n- **Backup cost facts** (for \"delete backups to save money\"); never claim a\\n  backup is free or that deleting it saves nothing:\\n  - All FSx backups are **incremental**; deleting one removes only the data\\n    unique to it, so the saving is that unique changed data, not the\\n    backup\\'s full size.\\n  - `AUTOMATIC` backups expire on their own after\\n    `AutomaticBackupRetentionDays`; `USER_INITIATED` and `AWS_BACKUP`\\n    backups are kept until someone deletes them, so they are the usual cost\\n    lever.\\n  - `AWS_BACKUP` backups can\\'t be deleted through the FSx console, CLI or\\n    API \u2014 the operator deletes them in AWS Backup.\\n  - For a cost question, also list the account\\'s `USER_INITIATED` and\\n    `AWS_BACKUP` backups in the Region whose volume or file system no longer\\n    exists (`describe-backups` with no filter; the source is gone from\\n    `describe-volumes`). They outlive their source and never expire, so they\\n    are often the real cost. Label them as outside the file system asked\\n    about, and state the recovery impact: the only copy of that data.\\n  - Source: [Protecting your data with volume backups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/using-backups.html).\\n- Backup failure causes and checks:\\n  [Troubleshooting FSx for ONTAP backups](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/fsx-ontap-troubleshoot-backups).\\n\\n## Item 10 \u2014 Alarms\\n\\n`cloudwatch:DescribeAlarms`, filtered to the fs-id. No alarm on SSD\\n`StorageCapacityUtilization` (and burst balance where it exists) \u2192 **LOW**\\nobservability gap. Recommend the alarm; never offer to create it.\\n\\n## Item 11 \u2014 Change history (CloudTrail)\\n\\nWindow: the Step 2 window (30 days when there is no incident). Cover FSx, EC2\\nsecurity-group, `ds`, KMS, and AWS Backup events\\n([cloudtrail-audit.md](cloudtrail-audit.md)).\\n\\n- **Query the file system\\'s own Region.** CloudTrail is regional: a lookup in\\n  another Region returns zero events, and that zero proves nothing.\\n- **Never use `AttributeKey=ResourceName` with an fs-, svm-, or fsvol- ID.**\\n  FSx events have an empty `Resources[]`, so that lookup always returns zero.\\n  Look up each mutating `EventName` (`UpdateFileSystem`, `UpdateVolume`,\\n  `UpdateStorageVirtualMachine`, `Delete*`) and filter with\\n  `contains(CloudTrailEvent, \\'<fs-id>\\')`. Add the `Create*` events\\n  (`CreateStorageVirtualMachine`, `CreateVolume`, `CreateFileSystem`) whenever\\n  a resource may have been broken **since creation** (MISCONFIGURED with no\\n  later Update): it has no Update/Delete history, and the Create call\\'s\\n  `requestParameters` is the evidence. `ResourceName` does work for EC2 IDs\\n  (sg-, rtb-, acl-).\\n- **Never use `AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=fsx.amazonaws.com`.** It\\n  returns every `Describe*`/`List*` call (including your own), 50 per page, so\\n  real changes fall off the first page.\\n- **Budget:** one call per `EventName` you need, `--start-time` at the window\\n  edge, first page only unless it is full *and* still inside the window. Don\\'t\\n  re-query the same `EventName` by another resource, and don\\'t widen the\\n  window hunting for a change: \"no matching events in the window\" is a finding.\\n- **Report every mutating event found** in a *Change history* table (time,\\n  event, caller, what changed, from `requestParameters`), including events by\\n  test or automation roles.\\n- **Link each change to the finding it explains** \u2014 e.g. an `UpdateFileSystem`\\n  that set `weeklyMaintenanceStartTime` is the origin of the window overlap.\\n  Never write \"no config changes\" if any mutating event is in the window.\\n- **A \"who changed this\" audit also covers dependency events** \u2014\\n  `DeleteDirectory`, `ds:` changes, and security-group `Authorize*`/`Revoke*`.\\n  Include them, or state plainly that only `fsx:` calls were in scope.\\n- Report a setting as \"removed\" only with a matching change event; otherwise\\n  describe the current state only.\\n\\n## Environment context\\n\\nRead the file system\\'s `Tags` (e.g. `Environment`, `Project`,\\n`aws:cloudformation:stack-name`) and state the inference explicitly (\"tags\\n`Project=\u2026` suggest a test environment\"). \"qbr-agent\"}]}]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_mOtT95mZdR7X6pp8fAbZrp", "content": "[{'text': '# CloudWatch Metrics \u2014 All FSx ONTAP Deployment Types\\n\\n**Sources:** public AWS FSx for NetApp ONTAP documentation (`docs.aws.amazon.com`). Public doc wins any conflict. Read-only, control-plane.\\n\\nAll metrics publish to the `AWS/FSx` namespace. Read this file before querying\\nor interpreting any metric. Failure-mode thresholds and severity live in\\n`REFERENCE.md` \u00a71\u2013\u00a73. This file covers **what each metric is, where it exists,\\nand how to query it** for each deployment type.\\n\\n## Quick rules (all types)\\n\\n1. Decide the generation from `DeploymentType` (`*_1` = gen1, `*_2` = gen2)\\n   before choosing dimensions (`deployment-types.md`).\\n2. Query every `*Utilization` metric on **`Maximum`**. FSx emits one datapoint\\n   per active file server or aggregate, even under `FileSystemId` alone, so\\n   `Average` hides a hot HA pair.\\n3. Empty series = **InsufficientData**, never zero or healthy. Run\\n   `cloudwatch:ListMetrics` for the file system to confirm which metric and\\n   dimension combinations exist before calling anything missing.\\n4. `Data*OperationTime` is in **seconds**. Average latency =\\n   Sum(`Data*OperationTime`) / Sum(`Data*Operations`) over the same period.\\n5. Gen2: locate the problem by `FileServer` / `Aggregate`, and size against\\n   **per-HA-pair** limits. Odd-numbered file servers carry client traffic.\\n   Even-numbered standbys still show background CPU and network, so a busy\\n   standby is not by itself evidence of failover.\\n\\n## Collection checklist (Step 2)\\n\\nMetric names are the same on\\nevery deployment type. Gen1 (Multi-AZ 1, Single-AZ 1) metrics take\\n`FileSystemId` (plus `VolumeId` / `StorageTier` / `DataType` where noted).\\n**Gen2** (Multi-AZ 2, Single-AZ 2) also publishes network, CPU, and\\nfile-server metrics per `FileServer` and disk / storage metrics per\\n`Aggregate`, and its utilization metrics are **% of one HA pair**. On every\\ntype, query `*Utilization` metrics on **`Maximum`**: FSx emits one datapoint\\nper active file server or aggregate, so `Average` hides a hot HA pair. On gen2,\\nuse `FileServer` / `Aggregate` to locate the hot pair. Odd-numbered file\\nservers carry client traffic, and even-numbered standbys still show background\\nload. See\\n\"Gen1 vs gen2 metrics\" below. Confirm what exists with\\n`cloudwatch:ListMetrics` before concluding a metric is missing.\\n- `StorageCapacityUtilization` \u2014 SSD tier fill % per aggregate (detailed metric,\\n  dimensions `StorageTier=SSD`, `DataType=All`; alert threshold: >75%)\\n- `FileServerDiskThroughputBalance` / `FileServerDiskIopsBalance` \u2014 % of\\n  **burst credits** remaining. Documented on the gen1 metrics page for\\n  throughput capacity **< 512 MBps**. Gen2 also emits them, per `FileSystemId` and per\\n  `FileServer`, even though the gen2 metrics page doesn\\'t list them (verified\\n  live at 384 MBps and at 1,536 MBps per HA pair). The performance table\\n  documents disk burst only for gen2 tiers up to 1,536 MBps per pair, so expect\\n  no balance series at 3,072 / 6,144 MBps per pair (unverified: check\\n  `ListMetrics`). A declining balance means the\\n  workload is bursting above baseline. Throttling to baseline occurs only as\\n  the balance approaches **0**. Do NOT treat <100% alone as throttling.\\n- `FileServerDiskThroughputUtilization` / `FileServerDiskIopsUtilization` \u2014\\n  file-server disk throughput / IOPS as % of the throughput-capacity limit\\n- `DiskIopsUtilization` \u2014 SSD IOPS as % of provisioned SSD IOPS\\n- `NetworkThroughputUtilization` \u2014 network saturation\\n- `CPUUtilization` \u2014 file-server CPU (use `AWS/FSx` metric only, not EC2-level)\\n- `DataReadBytes` / `DataWriteBytes` and `DataReadOperations` /\\n  `DataWriteOperations` \u2014 client I/O (Sum \u00f7 period seconds = per-second rate)\\n- `DataReadOperationTime` / `DataWriteOperationTime` \u2014 client latency\\n  (Sum \u00f7 Sum of matching Operations = average latency)\\n\\n\\n## Metric basics\\n\\nFrom\\n[Monitoring with CloudWatch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/monitoring-cloudwatch.html)\\nand [File system metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/file-system-metrics.html)):\\nall FSx for ONTAP metrics publish to the **`AWS/FSx`** namespace at **1-minute**\\nperiods, except `FileServerDiskThroughputBalance` and `FileServerDiskIopsBalance`\\nwhich publish at **5-minute** intervals; CloudWatch retains them for **15\\nmonths**. ## Relevant snippets

**§1 SSD Threshold Cascade:**
- "At 90%, data read from the capacity pool is **no longer cached** on the SSD tier"
- "At or above 98%, **all tiering stops** — even for volumes with tiering policy `ALL`."
- "Up to **16% of SSD is ONTAP overhead** (11% software + 5% aggregate snapshots; software portion drops to 6% above 30 TiB of SSD)."
- "Sizing guide: reserve roughly **1 GiB of SSD for every 10 GiB** of data you intend to keep on the capacity pool."
- "A backup can **fail** when the snapshot it needs would push the volume over **98%** SSD utilization"
- Snapshot spill: "CloudWatch `StorageUsed` per `VolumeId` with `StorageTier=All`, `DataType=Snapshot` (vs `DataType=User`)"

**§2 Throughput Capacity (Gen2, Multi-AZ 2 / Single-AZ 2):**
- "Second-generation network baseline **per HA pair**: 384 → 781, 768 → 1,563, 1,536 → 3,125, 3,072 → 6,250, 6,144 → 12,500 MB/s, with disk throughput equal to the tier (burst to 3,125 MB/s up to 1,536)."
- "384 and 768 are available only with one HA pair."
- "Gen2 tiers of 384, 768, and 1,536 MBps per HA pair burst disk throughput (to 3,125 MBps) and IOPS."
- "**Write ceiling below the provisioned throughput**"
- "A throughput-capacity change switches out the file server, causing an **automatic failover and failback** on **both Single-AZ and Multi-AZ** file systems, typically a few minutes"
- "On **second-generation** file systems a change starts a **6-hour cooldown** shared with SSD/IOPS scaling (the two cannot run at once)"
- "Burst-credit metrics: Gen2 tiers of 384, 768, and 1,536 MBps per HA pair burst disk throughput (to 3,125 MBps) and IOPS. 3,072 and 6,144 MBps have no documented burst"
- Sizing formula: "requirement = read MB/s + **2 × write MB/s** (writes are replicated to the partner file server and use twice the network)"
- "Pick the smallest tier whose **network baseline** covers the sustained requirement"

**§3 SSD IOPS Thresholds/Severity:**
- "`DiskIopsUtilization` sustained >= 95%": HIGH
- "85–95%": MEDIUM
- "< 85%": INFO
- "IOPS mode (`AUTOMATIC` vs `USER_PROVISIONED`) from `DescribeFileSystems`"
- "Provisioning SSD IOPS above the file server's baseline (e.g. 6,000 at 128 MBps Gen1) runs the server on IOPS burst credits (`FileServerDiskIopsBalance`)"
- "High `DiskIopsUtilization` with low client `DataReadOperations`/`DataWriteOperations` = background operations (SnapMirror, dedup, WAFL scanner) — NOT a client-impacting issue"

**§4 Tiering/Cooling-Period Guidance:**
- "`SNAPSHOT_ONLY`": Default; moves cold snapshots only (min 2-day cooling) | Active datasets
- "`AUTO`": Moves cold user data + snapshots (default 31-day cooling; range 2–183 days) | General workloads
- "`ALL`": Moves all data immediately (Cloud Write Mode) | Large migrations
- "`NONE`": No tiering; all data stays on SSD | Latency-sensitive hot volumes
- Policy `NONE` on a large archive/cold volume → SSD stays full unnecessarily. **MEDIUM/HIGH** depending on SSD pressure.
- Policy `ALL` on a hot volume → latency as active data reads from capacity pool. **MEDIUM**.
- Cooling period too long for the access pattern → cold data lingers on SSD. **LOW/MEDIUM**.

**§6 SG Port Requirements:**
- "| 2049 | TCP/UDP | NFS |"
- "| 635 | TCP/UDP | mountd |"
- "| 111 | TCP/UDP | portmapper (NFSv3) |"
- "| 445 | TCP | SMB |"
- "These are the only ports clients need **inbound to the FSx file system** to mount/access shares."
- "**Active Directory ports (389, 88, 464, 53, 636, 3268/3269) are NOT inbound client→FSx rules.** They carry traffic from the **SVM to the domain controllers**"
- Multi-AZ routing: "A client whose subnet's route table is **not** in `RouteTableIds` cannot reach the endpoints, or loses access after a failover."
- "FSx creates **one /32 route per floating IP** (`1 + number of SVMs`: management plus each SVM's NFS/SMB endpoint), targeting the **preferred subnet's ENI**, **only in the route tables listed in `OntapConfiguration.RouteTableIds`**"
- "**iSCSI and intercluster (SnapMirror) endpoints are not floating.** They are in-VPC IPs, one per subnet."

**§7 False-Signal Suppression Rules:**
- "**EC2-level CPU on the file servers reads ~99–100% at all times.** ONTAP does not release vCPUs when idle. Never use instance-level CPU as evidence of saturation; only the `AWS/FSx` `CPUUtilization` metric is meaningful."
- "**Throughput scaling stuck `IN_PROGRESS` (AdministrativeActions).** During a throughput-capacity scale, the preferred (serving) file server scales first and immediately serves traffic at the NEW throughput... the customer already has the requested throughput"
- "**Insufficient-capacity errors (ICE) on scaling operations** — the remedy is to retry the operation until it succeeds; there is no configuration fix."
- "**A daily automatic backup was skipped** — if the file system's maintenance window overlaps its backup window, maintenance (patching) takes priority... Finding is the **WINDOW OVERLAP** (MEDIUM, fix: separate the windows)"
- "**Tiering that has not moved data yet** — tiering moves only data that is cold per the volume's policy and cooling period, and pauses when SSD is too full (§1, §4)... AWS publishes no aggregate-utilization percentage at which tiering begins, so do not state one."
- "**Closed ports for a protocol the incident does not involve**... If those ports were never part of the baseline and that protocol is not in use, record at most an INFO observation, not a finding."

**§8 Maintenance-Window Behavior/Failover:**
- "**Failover / failback** ([Failover process](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/ONTAPGuide/high-availability-AZ.html#Failover)): automatic on **all** deployment types and typically completes in < 60 seconds. Multi-AZ fails back automatically, usually in < 60 seconds."
- "Triggers: file-server failure, throughput change, planned maintenance, and AZ outage (Multi-AZ only)."
- "Transparent to NFS/SMB because the endpoint IP is unchanged. iSCSI / NVMe/TCP depend on client multipathing."
- "Patching/upgrade failures: check SSD free space first (a nearly-full SSD tier blocks maintenance), then whether the maintenance window elapsed before completion."

**§9 Baseline/Pre-Event Checklist:**
- "1. **SSD utilization posture** against the skill's severity bands... and AWS's behavioral thresholds (80% recommended maximum, 90% capacity-pool read caching stops, 98% tiering stops) (§1). Per aggregate on gen2."
- "2. **Throughput and IOPS headroom** — 7-day p95 of §2/§3 metrics against provisioned values."
- "3. **Tiering policy vs observed access** — per-volume policy/cooling period vs per-tier capacity split (§4)."
- "4. **Backup posture** — automatic daily backups enabled, retention matches stated RPO, backup window does NOT overlap the maintenance window (§7), recent backups actually present **per volume** (`DescribeBackups` filtered by `volume-id`)"
- "5. **Snapshot hygiene** — stale snapshots, count growth, reserve pressure (§1)."
- "6. **Resilience shape** — deployment type vs the workload's stated availability requirement... For Multi-AZ: every client subnet's route table is in `RouteTableIds`, and off-VPC clients come through Transit Gateway (§6)."
- "7. **Protocol/AD posture** — SVM protocol enablement and AD join state vs what clients actually use (§6)."
- "8. **Version currency** — ONTAP version and pending `AdministrativeActions`; note the 9.14.1 SnapMirror behavior change (§5) when an upgrade is planned.""}]}], "label": "Extract throughput, IOPS, tiering and baseline guidance"}

   - **Metrics:** The file system was created Nov 2. In the 7 days of metrics, every read and write counter is zero, so nothing here predicts batch behavior. Peaks over the week:

     | Metric | Peak |
     |---|---|
     | CPU | 20% |
     | Network | 1.2% |
     | Disk throughput | 2.1% |
     | `DiskIopsUtilization` | 6.7% |

     Disk throughput and IOPS burst balances sit at 99%.
   - **Ceilings that apply:**
     - Throughput capacity is **384 MBps** per HA pair.
     - The network baseline for that tier is about **781 MB/s**. Disk throughput can burst up to 3,125 MBps while credits last.
     - SSD IOPS is **3,072**. This is Automatic mode, which gives 3 IOPS per GiB on 1,024 GiB.
   - **Which limit binds:** For random-I/O-heavy batch work, the 3,072 IOPS ceiling is the one most likely to bind first. For streaming work it is the 384 MBps disk baseline, with burst credits as a buffer.
   - **Sizing check:** Estimated network demand is read MB/s plus 2 × write MB/s (writes are replicated to the standby), and it should stay under about 781 MB/s.
   - **Timing of any change:** A throughput capacity change forces a failover and failback of a few minutes. On this generation, throughput, SSD capacity and IOPS changes share a 6-hour cooldown. If the numbers look tight, make the change this week rather than the day of the run.

6. **LOW (unverified): the batch clients' network path.**
   - **Route tables:** The route table `rtb-00000000000000007` is in `RouteTableIds` and covers both file system subnets. That is correct for clients in those subnets. I can't see your client subnets.
   - **Security group:** `sg-00000000000000012` allows NFS (2049, 111, 635, 4045–4046), SMB (445) and ICMP, but only from one source security group, `sg-00000000000000013`. Batch hosts that aren't in that group, or that connect from on-premises, through a VPN or Direct Connect, or from a peered or Transit Gateway VPC without CIDR rules, would be silently dropped.

The failure is an authentication failure for the AD service account `Admin`. It is not a connectivity or missing-directory problem.
- **Password reset:** the reset of `Admin` at 22:44:58 came one minute before the 22:45:58 retry, which still failed. Either the SVM was given a password that doesn't match what was set, or the new password hadn't propagated to both domain controllers yet. CloudTrail hides the password, so I can't tell which.
- **Initial create:** the CreateStorageVirtualMachine at 17:05:20 was issued by CloudFormation at the same moment as the directory and file system build. The SVM was first built with the CloudFormation-supplied password, and it may never have worked.
